terra.problem: Calling the treasures David's own does not establish that they weren't leftovers.
David gives his delight as his reason, but the text does not establish that nobody urged him to give.
David names delight as his reason, but the text does not say whether anyone requested the gift.
The passage does not say whether David came to the assembly with a sword.
The leaders gave willingly, but the text does not say whether anyone had urged them to give.
The imagined dancing places Papa Dorin in the Bible event with the assembly.
The cookie comparison puts the person who baked and gave the cookie in God's role, rather than keeping the comparison on the human side.
The passage records David's prayer that Solomon build the palace; it does not say here that Solomon will build it.
The explanation presents Solomon's building as an accomplished fact, while this passage records David's prayer for him to build.
The explanation is a mechanical restatement, ending with 'the statement is true as written' rather than sounding like Papa Dorin.
Saying Zadok 'takes the priest's role' suggests he is newly taking the role. The passage says he is anointed as priest, not when he became a priest.
The reference given does not establish that Eli himself was a priest. 1 Samuel 1:9 identifies him as one.
Solomon's prosperity and Israel's obedience do not establish that the beginning of his reign was peaceful.
The explanation repeats the statement and closes with test-checking language rather than Papa Dorin's voice.
The text says Solomon's royal majesty was unlike what had been bestowed on earlier kings; it does not explicitly say it was 'more than' theirs.
The explanation says the thirty-three years add up to forty. The forty-year total includes both the seven and the thirty-three years.
The passage does not say David saw Solomon sitting on the throne.
The text does not say the opposite of David dying alone or in the palace. It describes his age, riches and honor, and records where his acts are written.
